name: Tuojiang Riverside Core
tagline: The postcard heart of the ancient town
description: The famous stretch of diaojiaolou stilt houses lining the Tuojiang, threaded with cobbled lanes, weirs, and stepping stones. This is Fenghuang at its most beautiful and its most crowded, glowing with lantern light and reflections after dark, ringed by guesthouses, souvenir stalls, and riverside cafes.
bestFor: Sightseeing, photography, and short scenic stays
cons: Very crowded and noisy at night

name: Hong Bridge and North Gate
tagline: Historic arches and the old city wall
description: The area around the covered Hong Bridge and the North Gate tower, where the old city wall meets the river. A dense, historic quarter of stone gates, arched crossings, and busy lanes, it packs in heritage landmarks and pours out crowds toward the water each evening.

name: New Town Outside the Walls
tagline: Everyday Fenghuang beyond the scenic zone
description: The ordinary modern town spreading beyond the old walls, with local shops, apartments, buses, and cheaper eateries. Far less charming than the riverside, it offers calmer, more affordable long-stay rooms, genuine local life, and a practical base away from the relentless tourist bustle.
cons: Short walk or ride to the sights

name: Rail Station Road and Miao Villages
tagline: Gateway to fast trains and minority country
description: The corridor toward the Fenghuang Ancient Town high-speed rail station and the surrounding Xiangxi countryside dotted with Miao villages. Spread out and workaday near the station, it opens onto green hills, terraced fields, and cultural day trips beyond the town's commercial core.
vibe: Transitional, rural-edged, and convenient for travel
bestFor: Rail connections and rural cultural day trips
pros: Fast trains toward Zhangjiajie and Huaihua
Access to Miao villages and countryside
cons: Away from the riverside old town
